newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ming Wah sees better 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Ming Wah sees better 1996 profits.

text.p: Ship-owning and chartering company Ming Wah Universal (Bermuda) Co Ltd said on Thursday it expects better profits this year.
"We believe profits this year are going to be better than last year," said Wong Hong Ming, general manager of the commercial division.

"Profit for the first six months of this year was better than last year by about 20 percent. I believe performance in the second half will to continue to do well," Wong said at a signing ceremony for the purchase of two tankers, worth US$86 million.
In September, Ming Wah reported net profit for the first six months ended June 1996 grew 20 percent to Singapore $4.81 million on a turnover of S$17.73 million.
Ming Wah is a unit of Hong Kong-listed China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Ltd.
Executive director To Wing Sing said the company planned to expand its fleet by buying second-hand vessels or building new ones.
It now has six vessels -- a Very Large Ore Carrier (VLOC) and five Aframax tankers of 89,000 deadweight tonnes each used to carry crude oil and refined products.
